chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the udhiyah in Mina, and he said: four days. And about the udhiyah in the rest of the towns, he said: the udhiyah is three days.
3—Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ghiyath, from Ja'far, from his father عليهما السلام, from Ali عليه السلام, who said:
The udhiyah is three days, and the best of them is the first of them.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَيَّامٍ: a legal period of four days
key_terms.أَفْضَلُهَا: the most virtuous among those days
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: the period of udhiyah and sacrifice during Eid al-Adha
key_terms.بِمِنًى: in Mina, the hajj locality where sacrificial rites are performed
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: a legal period of three days

ai.seo_question: How many days does the udhiyah last in Mina and in other towns?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal duration of the days of udhiyah and sacrifice: four days in Mina and three days in other towns. It also states that among these days, the first day is the most excellent.
